name: SISO Knowledge boundary and reallocation inventory

preservation.reason: The Knowledge checkout contains substantial pre-existing corpus, pipeline, index, operator, and nested-repository work. The public architecture commit is safe, but dirty source must be bridged or committed by its owner before further physical moves.

nested_repositories.preservation: Preserve the deployable web product and its local data coupling before filing it with the product estate.
Preserve extensive UI work before assigning a shared product or design-system home.
Independent clean Research Work; represent it through registry relationships rather than physical containment.
Independent Research Work with one preserved local edit; do not move until bridged.
Clean historical source checkout; preserve its history while replacing physical nesting with an evidence locator later.

units.name: Canonical knowledge corpus and schemas
units.rationale: These paths hold atomic knowledge records, cross-page synthesis, and the canonical hierarchy contracts; they directly serve the Work outcome.

evidence.summary: The published domain manifest assigns authored corpus and schema authority to these zones.

units.name: Acquisition, curation, query, and maintenance tools
units.target: SISO Knowledge until independent adoption justifies a split
units.rationale: The tools implement the Knowledge lifecycle; size or file count alone is not evidence for separate repository identity.

evidence.summary: Pipeline, query, and maintenance entrypoints were classified by responsibility, with acquired payloads separated into the data plane.

units.name: Generated indexes and graph projections
units.rationale: Indexes and graphs provide retrieval views over canonical records; they are generated projections, not independent Works or hand-authored truth.

evidence.summary: The data contract names rebuild commands and generated authority.

units.name: Knowledge-specific feeder and curator operators
units.target: Keep Knowledge-specific definitions; move generic capabilities to Agents and runtime state to private storage
units.rationale: Operator purpose belongs with Knowledge, but generic skills, live memory, heartbeat, inbox, outbox, and machine routes are not canonical knowledge source.

evidence.summary: Identities, hooks, skills, memory, heartbeat, and workspace files were separated conceptually and tracked as explicit compatibility debt.

units.name: Foundry and Evidence Engines
units.rationale: Both systems have independent outcomes, Git histories, public repositories, releases, and consumers; local placement does not imply containment.

evidence.summary: The whole-Library projection keeps all three Research Works independently pinned and related.

units.name: Legacy Knowledge web product
units.target: SISO Agency product estate after a preservation bridge
units.rationale: This is a deployable Next.js product rather than durable knowledge source, but its dirty state and local data coupling block a safe move today.

evidence.summary: Package, deployment role, remote, and dirty state identify an application boundary exception.

units.name: Shared design system
units.target: Shared SISO product and UI ownership after a preservation bridge
units.rationale: The component bank, viewer, CLI, and MCP package serve multiple products and do not implement knowledge production; extensive dirty work blocks an immediate move.

evidence.summary: The nested repository role, remote, and dirty state were directly verified.

units.name: Historical source awaiting evidence-led promotion
units.target: Provenance-preserving source inventories, not canonical corpus
units.rationale: Historical source may contain valuable material but must retain origin, rights, and history until individual units pass promotion gates.

evidence.summary: The published boundary guide forbids treating inventories as canonical knowledge by default.
The public boundary release preserves the mixed local checkout while publishing only reviewed structure, policies, and receipts.
Moved legacy units, retired compatibility naming, preserved archive destinations, and deliberate boundary exceptions are recorded.
